title: Can a Shrimp's Snap Get as HOT as the SUN? 🦐
description:
Snap your fingers. Cute. Now meet the pistol shrimp: it snaps one giant claw shut so fast that it shoots out a jet of water (about 90 km/h) and tears the water open into a bubble. The bang isn't the claw hitting anything: it's that bubble crushing itself, one of the loudest animal sounds in the sea. For a split second, the inside of the bubble gets nearly as hot as the surface of the Sun (at least about 4,700 °C, against roughly 5,500 °C for the Sun's surface), and it gives off a flash of light far too faint for your eyes. Scientists really did name it shrimpoluminescence. And in World War Two, the crackle of whole reefs of these shrimp scrambled the sonar the Navy used to hunt submarines. Who wins a snap-off: you or the shrimp?
